notes:
All bitmap/metric numbers below were verified by downloading vanilla `assets/minecraft/textures/font/ascii.png` (via the misode/mcmeta assets mirror) and inspecting pixel alpha directly, plus reading the decompiled 1.8 `FontRenderer.java` for the rendering algorithm. Where modern (1.19/1.20) code differs I flag it.

## 1. Glyph geometry (verified from ascii.png, 128x128, 16x16 grid of 8x8 cells)

Cell row/col for codepoint `cp`: `row = cp >> 4`, `col = cp & 15`, pixel origin `(col*8, row*8)`.

Vertical layout inside the 8-px cell (y measured down from the cell top; `ascent = 7` â‡’ baseline is the boundary between row 6 and row 7):
```
row 0  â”€â”€ cap line / ascender line
row 1
row 2  â”€â”€ x-height line
row 3
row 4
row 5
row 6  â”€â”€ last row above baseline
â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€ baseline (y = 7 from cell top)
row 7  â”€â”€ descender row (1 px only)
```
- Caps + digits: rows 0..6 â†’ cap height **7 px**
- Ascenders (b d f h k l t, dot of i/j): rows 0..6 â†’ **7 px**
- x-height letters (a c e m n o r s u v w x z): rows 2..6 â†’ **5 px**
- Descenders (g j p q y and `,` `;`): reach row 7 â†’ **1 px** below baseline
- `j` is the only ASCII glyph spanning the full 0..7 (8 px)
- Stroke weight is **1 px everywhere**. There are zero 2-px strokes in ASCII.

## 2. Advance widths â€” exact algorithm

```
inkWidth(c)  = 1 + max{ x : column x of the 8x8 cell has any pixel with alpha > 0 }   (0 if empty)
advance(c)   = inkWidth(c) + 1                     // the +1 IS the inter-glyph gap
advance(' ') = 4                                   // from the `space` provider, cell is blank
advance(c, bold) = advance(c) + 1
width(str)   = Î£ advance(c)                        // includes a trailing 1 px gap after the last glyph
```
1.8 used an alpha threshold of `> 16`; the wiki documents modern as `> 0`. For a general bitmap provider with declared `height` H and physical cell height Ph the ink width is scaled: `advance = round(inkWidth * H / Ph) + 1`. For ascii.png H = Ph = 8 so scale is 1.

Full ASCII inkâ†’advance table (ink / advance, px):
```
' ' â€“/4   ! 1/2   " 3/4   # 5/6   $ 5/6   % 5/6   & 5/6   ' 1/2
(  3/4    ) 3/4   * 3/4   + 5/6   , 1/2   - 5/6   . 1/2   / 5/6
0-9 5/6   : 1/2   ; 1/2   < 4/5   = 5/6   > 4/5   ? 5/6   @ 6/7
A-H 5/6   I 3/4   J-Z 5/6
[  3/4    \ 5/6   ] 3/4   ^ 5/6   _ 5/6   ` 2/3
a-e 5/6   f 4/5   g 5/6   h 5/6   i 1/2   j 5/6   k 4/5   l 2/3
m-s 5/6   t 3/4   u-z 5/6
{  3/4    | 1/2   } 3/4   ~ 6/7
```
Sanity checks: `width("a") == 6`, `width("i") == 2`, `width(" ") == 4`, `width("@") == 7`, `width("hello") == 6+6+3+6+6 = 27`.

## 3. Rendering pipeline (per line)

```
pen_x = x; y = top-of-line
if (dropShadow) render whole line at (x+1, y+1) with shadowColor  // drawn FIRST, behind
render whole line at (x, y) with fgColor

per glyph:
  draw 8x8 cell quad with top-left at (pen_x, y)      // ink lands in the cell's own coords
  if (bold) draw the same quad again at (pen_x+1, y); adv += 1
  if (strikethrough) fillRect(pen_x, y+3, adv, 1)     // legacy exact; modern y+3.5..y+4.5, x from pen_x-1
  if (underline)     fillRect(pen_x-1, y+8, adv+1, 1)
  pen_x += adv
next line: y += 9
```

### Shadow colour
```js
shadow = (fg & 0xFF000000) | ((fg & 0x00FCFCFC) >>> 2);
```
The `0xFC` mask before the shift is load-bearing: it prevents low bits of one channel bleeding into the next and makes 0xFF â†’ 0x3F (63), **not** 64. Confirmed in 1.8 source as `color = (color & 16579836) >> 2 | color & -16777216;`.

Vanilla Â§-colour shadow pairs (fg â†’ shadow) all satisfy this except Â§6 gold, whose shadow is hardcoded #3E2A00 rather than the computed #3F2A00 (FFAA00 & FCFCFC = FCA800, >>2 = 3F2A00). Treat gold as a special case if you want byte-exact parity.

### Italic
1.8 quad vertices with `s = italic ? 1 : 0`:
```
topLeft  = (pen_x + s,               y)
botLeft  = (pen_x - s,               y + 7.99)
topRight = (pen_x + 6.99 + s,        y)
botRight = (pen_x + 6.99 - s,        y + 7.99)
```
i.e. a shear of **Â±1 px** about the vertical centre â†’ **2 px total lean over 8 px**, slope 0.25. Modern `BakedGlyph.render` uses `0.25F * up / 0.25F * down` coefficients â€” same 0.25 slope, but anchored differently (bottom-anchored rather than centre-anchored), so a modern-faithful clone leans the top +2 px and leaves the bottom at 0. Advance is **not** changed by italic, so italic text overlaps slightly and can clip 1â€“2 px past the measured width. In CSS terms: `transform: skewX(-14deg)` â‰ˆ slope 0.25 (atan(0.25) = 14.04Â°).

### Obfuscated Â§k
1.8 exact:
```java
int i = index_of_original_glyph;
int j;
do { j = fontRandom.nextInt(charWidth.length); } while ((int)charWidth[i] != (int)charWidth[j]);
draw glyph j;
```
Uniform rejection sampling over the *whole* glyph table restricted to equal (truncated-to-int) advance. Modern buckets glyphs by `Mth.ceil(advance)` into `FontSet.glyphsByWidth` and picks with `RandomSource`. Consequences for a clone:
- Build `Map<advance, glyph[]>` once; on each frame pick `pool[floor(rand()*pool.length)]`.
- Re-roll **per rendered frame**, not per tick â€” vanilla just calls the renderer again each frame, so at unlocked FPS it flickers as fast as you draw.
- String width is unchanged, so layout/wrapping stays stable.
- Selection is per-glyph-position, independent between characters.
- Modern (1.13+) draws from all Unicode glyphs the font has, not just ASCII, so you'll see box-drawing/Greek/Cyrillic shapes.

### Reset semantics
`Â§r` clears colour AND all five style flags. A colour code (`Â§0`â€“`Â§f`) also implicitly resets bold/italic/underline/strike/obfuscated in Java Edition legacy parsing. Style flags reset at the start of every string render.

## 4. Font provider JSON (1.20 `minecraft:default`)
```
default.json â†’ [ reference include/space, reference include/default {filter:{uniform:false}}, reference include/unifont ]
include/space.json â†’ { "type":"space", "advances": { " ": 4, "â€Œ": 0 } }
include/default.json â†’ bitmap nonlatin_european.png (ascent 7, height default 8, 8x8 cells, 16x67)
                     â†’ bitmap accented.png (height 12, ascent 10, 9x12 cells, 16x75)
                     â†’ bitmap ascii.png (ascent 7, height default 8, 8x8 cells, 16x16)
```
`accented.png` sits 3 px higher (ascent 10 vs 7 in a 12-px box) so accents clear the cap line by 3 px and the box extends 2 px below baseline; baselines still align because the provider positions by ascent.

## 5. Exact letterforms (dumped from vanilla ascii.png) â€” for hand-authoring a lookalike

Design rules the whole face obeys:
- **Strictly 1-px stroke, no antialiasing, no curves.** "Round" shapes are rectangles with the 4 corner pixels omitted (`o` = 5x5 box minus corners).
- **Diagonals are 1-px stair-steps**, used only in `k v w x y(no) z N V W X Z % / \ 0 & $ ?` and the shoulder joins of `b h m n p r`.
- Lowercase shoulders (`b h m n p r`) use a distinctive **1-px diagonal knee**: `#.##.` over `##..#`.
- Terminals of `l` and `t` **kick 1 px to the right** at the baseline row â€” this is the single most Minecraft-identifying detail.
- `g`, `y`, `j` share one **left-sweeping tail**: `....#` at row 6 then `####.` at row 7.

```
A (5x7)      a (5x5)      g (5x6)      e (5x5)      s (5x5)
.###.        .###.        .####        .###.        .####
#...#        ....#        #...#        #...#        #....
#####        .####        #...#        #####        .###.
#...#        #...#        .####        #....        ....#
#...#        .####        ....#        .####        ####.
#...#                     ####.
#...#

t (3x7)      y (5x6)      i (1x7)      l (2x7)      o (5x5)
.#.          #...#        #            #            .###.
.#.          #...#        .            #            #...#
###          #...#        #            #            #...#
.#.          .####        #            #            #...#
.#.          ....#        #            #            .###.
.#.          ####.        #            #
..#                       #            .#

0 (5x7)      k (4x7)      f (4x7)      m (5x5)      r (5x5)
.###.        #...         ..##         ##.#.        #.##.
#...#        #...         .#..         #.#.#        ##..#
#..##        #..#         ####         #.#.#        #....
#.#.#        #.#.         .#..         #...#        #....
##..#        ##..         .#..         #...#        #....
#...#        #.#.         .#..
.###.        #..#         .#..
```
Notable identity marks: `a` is **single-storey with no left stem at the top** (top bar floats, bowl closes at the bottom); `e` has a **full-width 5-px crossbar** and a solid left wall; `s` is built from two 4-px bars offset by 1; `t`'s crossbar is only 3 px and sits at the x-height line; `0` carries an **internal diagonal slash**; `M` and `W` use a **2-row-deep** middle vertex; `i` has **no serifs at all** (pure 1-px stem + 1-px dot with a 1-px gap); `,` and `;` are 1 px wide and drop into the descender row.

## 6. Practical clone checklist
1. Author a 128x128 PNG, 16x16 cells of 8x8, top-left aligned ink, alpha 0 background.
2. Precompute `advance[cp] = inkWidth+1` at load by scanning columns right-to-left for alpha>0; hardcode `advance[0x20]=4`.
3. Render at integer GUI scale (2x/3x/4x) with `image-rendering: pixelated` and nearest-neighbour sampling; never sample at fractional texel offsets or the 1-px strokes shimmer.
4. Word-wrap by accumulating advances and breaking at â‰¤ the container width in *font pixels*, then multiplying by GUI scale.
5. Draw order per line: shadow pass at (+1,+1) â†’ main pass â†’ effect rects (effects also need a shadow copy if the text has a shadow; vanilla renders effects inside each pass).
6. Bold changes measured width â€” measure with the bold flag applied or your centred text drifts.

## 7. Legally-safe font options, ranked by resemblance
1. **Minecraft-Font** (IdreesInc), OFL-1.1 â€” proportional rendition, closest metrics to Mojangles.
2. **Monocraft** (IdreesInc), OFL-1.1 â€” same designer, monospaced, 5x7 design grid; adds tails/serifs to `i`/`l` so it reads slightly less "Minecraft".
3. **Silkscreen** (Jason Kottke), OFL-1.1, on Google Fonts â€” 1-px stroke, orthogonal, similar x-height ratio; the safest "just link it" option.
4. **Pixel Operator** (Jayvee Enaguas), **CC0-1.0** â€” zero attribution burden; "Pixel Operator 8" is an 8-px face that maps almost 1:1 onto an 8-px cell grid.
5. **Departure Mono** (Helena Zhang), OFL-1.1 â€” 1-px stroke, 775 glyphs, pixel-perfect at multiples of 11 px; techier/wider than Mojangles.
6. **GNU Unifont**, GPLv2+font-exception / OFL-1.1 â€” use it as your CJK fallback exactly as Minecraft does (16-px cells).

Avoid **Minecraftia** (Andrew Tyler): personal-use only, commercial licence sold separately. Avoid extracting/redistributing `ascii.png` itself â€” it is an all-rights-reserved Mojang asset.

Given a hand-authored 8x8 grid, the whole face is ~95 glyphs at 1-px stroke; using the exact metrics above (cap 7 / x-height 5 / descender 1 / advance = ink+1 / line 9) gives pixel-identical layout to vanilla even with your own letterforms, which is the legally clean way to get a faithful clone.
